title: Jump Set of an Epipelagic Point
body_html:
Jump Set of an Epipelagic Point

Let \(L\) be the self-dual lattice function corresponding to an epipelagic point \(x\) of order \(m\). If \(G\) splits over a tame extension with ramification index \(m\), then \[ \operatorname{Jump}(L)\subseteq (1/m)\mathbb Z \] or \[ \operatorname{Jump}(L)\subseteq 1/(2m)+(1/m)\mathbb Z. \]
proof_html: After tame base change, \(x\) becomes hyperspecial, so the base-changed lattice function has jumps in one coset of \((1/m)\mathbb Z\). Self-duality forces the coset to be invariant under negation, leaving only the two possibilities \(0\) and \(1/(2m)\) modulo \((1/m)\mathbb Z\).
